tool_args.rationale: The supply-bullwhip bridge and flux-conservation signatures favor the archived two-layer siphon. All five pilot rows vary inflow at the same sink gradient, so they constrain the inflow curve but cannot separate maximum flux from sink inhibition. The open-branch probe is the cheapest targeted way to resolve that ambiguity before confirmation.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit the transferred two-layer siphon with a negative square-root branch
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The pilot favors this branch, but at s_grad = 1 it identifies only vmax × (1 − rho/2). Fixing rho from the archive would assume that sink sensitivity transfers unchanged.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit a two-layer siphon with linear leakage
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Linear leakage fits the pilot curvature less well and leaves the same sink-sensitivity ambiguity.
The unresolved question is sensitivity to the sink gradient, not time resolution. The targeted probe costs less.
